---
title: "04_reshape_couple_wide"
output: html_document
---

## Overview

Reshapes the person-level IPW baseline data (`ipw_sample.rds`, produced by
script 03) into a **one-row-per-couple wide format** (`ipw_wide.rds`) required
by the MICE imputation in script 05.

**Input:** `data/derived/ipw_sample.rds` — person-level baseline covariates
(two rows per couple: one male, one female).

**Outputs** (to `data/derived/`):

- `ipw_wide.rds` — one row per couple with male-prefixed (`M_`) and
  female-prefixed (`F_`) individual covariates plus shared household
  covariates. Read by script 05 (`05_mice_imputation_clean.Rmd`).
- `couple_key.csv` — crosswalk between the string `couple_id` and a numeric
  `couple_id_num` used in downstream Mplus export.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(here)

options(scipen = 999)

# zap_labels drops any haven_labelled attributes that rode along from the raw
# SOEP files through 03's joins; otherwise replace_na() downstream errors
# trying to coerce a labelled column.
ipw_sample <- readRDS(here("data", "derived", "ipw_sample.rds")) %>%
  zap_labels()

individual_vars <- c(
  "age", "life_sat", "germborn", "migration", "germcitz",
  "employment", "edu_level"
)

household_vars <- c(
  "hinc", "hgowner", "size", "smallspace", "livedhere",
  "east", "hhgr", "rel_duration", "syear"
)
```

## Verify shared household/couple covariates

```{r shared-check}
# These variables are later taken from one partner's baseline row only.
# Before doing so, verify that male and female values are identical within
# every couple, including their missingness pattern.

shared_check <- ipw_sample %>%
  select(
    couple_id,
    sex,
    all_of(household_vars)
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = all_of(household_vars),
    names_glue = "{.value}_sex{sex}"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(shared_check) == n_distinct(ipw_sample$couple_id)
)

shared_mismatch <- purrr::map_dfr(
  household_vars,
  function(v) {

    male_value   <- shared_check[[paste0(v, "_sex1")]]
    female_value <- shared_check[[paste0(v, "_sex2")]]

    mismatch <- (
      xor(is.na(male_value), is.na(female_value))
    ) | (
      !is.na(male_value) &
        !is.na(female_value) &
        abs(male_value - female_value) > 1e-8
    )

    tibble(
      variable = v,
      n_mismatch = sum(mismatch),
      pct_mismatch = 100 * mean(mismatch)
    )
  }
)

cat("\n--- SHARED HOUSEHOLD/COUPLE VARIABLE CHECK ---\n")
print(shared_mismatch)

if (any(shared_mismatch$n_mismatch > 0)) {

  bad_variables <- shared_mismatch %>%
    filter(n_mismatch > 0) %>%
    pull(variable)

  stop(
    "Male and female baseline rows disagree on shared variables: ",
    paste(bad_variables, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

cat("All shared household/couple covariates are identical within couples.\n")
```

## Reshape to one row per couple

```{r reshape-wide}
male_data <- ipw_sample %>%
  filter(sex == 1) %>%
  select(couple_id, all_of(individual_vars)) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0("M_", .), all_of(individual_vars))

female_data <- ipw_sample %>%
  filter(sex == 2) %>%
  select(couple_id, all_of(individual_vars)) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0("F_", .), all_of(individual_vars))

# Household/couple covariates are shared within dyad at baseline, so one
# partner's row is sufficient after the baseline HID consistency check in 03.
couple_data <- ipw_sample %>%
  filter(sex == 1) %>%
  select(couple_id, group, all_of(household_vars))

ipw_wide <- couple_data %>%
  inner_join(male_data,   by = "couple_id") %>%
  inner_join(female_data, by = "couple_id")

# One row per couple is assumed everywhere downstream.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ipw_wide$couple_id))

# Lock the sample counts inherited from the final 03 build.
stopifnot(
  nrow(ipw_wide) == 1602,
  sum(ipw_wide$group == 1) == 709,
  sum(ipw_wide$group == 0) == 893
)

cat("Rows:", nrow(ipw_wide), " Columns:", ncol(ipw_wide), "\n")
cat("Parent couples:",        sum(ipw_wide$group == 1), "\n")
cat("Non-parenting couples:", sum(ipw_wide$group == 0), "\n")
```

## Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
cat("M_germcitz:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$M_germcitz, useNA = "always"))

cat("F_germcitz:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$F_germcitz, useNA = "always"))

cat("M_germborn:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$M_germborn, useNA = "always"))

cat("hgowner:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$hgowner, useNA = "always"))

cat("smallspace:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$smallspace, useNA = "always"))

cat("east:\n")
print(table(ipw_wide$east, useNA = "always"))

cat("\nMissingness before exclusion:\n")

ipw_wide %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "var",
    values_to = "n_missing"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_missing)) %>%
  print(n = 40)

cat("\nCitizenship missingness in wide file:\n")
cit_missing <- colSums(
  is.na(ipw_wide[, c("M_germcitz", "F_germcitz")])
)
print(cit_missing)

stopifnot(
  cit_missing[["M_germcitz"]] == 0,
  cit_missing[["F_germcitz"]] == 0
)

cat("\nCouples (no exclusion):", nrow(ipw_wide), "\n")
cat("  Parent couples:",        sum(ipw_wide$group == 1), "\n")
cat("  Non-parenting couples:", sum(ipw_wide$group == 0), "\n")
```

## Save couple-level data and ID crosswalk

```{r save}
# Build the couple_id <-> numeric ID crosswalk exactly once here.
# Downstream files must reuse this mapping rather than recreating numeric IDs.
couple_key <- ipw_wide %>%
  distinct(couple_id) %>%
  mutate(couple_id_num = as.integer(factor(couple_id)))

stopifnot(
  nrow(couple_key) == nrow(ipw_wide),
  !anyDuplicated(couple_key$couple_id_num)
)

dir.create(
  here("data", "derived"),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

saveRDS(
  ipw_wide,
  here("data", "derived", "ipw_wide.rds")
)

write.csv(
  couple_key,
  here("data", "derived", "couple_key.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat(
  "Saved data/derived/ipw_wide.rds —",
  nrow(ipw_wide), "couples,",
  ncol(ipw_wide), "columns\n"
)

cat(
  "Saved data/derived/couple_key.csv —",
  nrow(couple_key), "couple IDs\n"
)
```
